raw.details:
STEM FOR IMPACT 2026 — HACKATHON CONFIRMATION & RULES

Hey everyone!

Thank you for registering for the STEM FOR IMPACT – 24 HRS HACKATHON

To finalize your participation, every registered team must complete the Confirmation Form below.

STEM FOR IMPACT HACKATHON – CONFIRMATION FORM
https://forms.gle/5XSeCbeR86bSpBZU9

️ IMPORTANT:
Only teams that complete and submit this Confirmation Form will be considered confirmed participants for the hackathon.

Registration alone does not confirm your participation.
Confirmation Form submission = Team Confirmation

STEM FOR IMPACT 2026 — RULES

Eligibility

  • Engineering students only
  • Teams must have exactly 5 members
  • One participant can register in only one team.
  • Institution Name is mandatory.

Registration

  • Internal: ₹500/team
  • External: ₹1,000/team
  • Fee is per team, not per participant.

 Hackathon

17–18 November 2026 | 24 Hours
E Block, 4th Floor Hall, Presidency University, Bangalore

  • Teams will select from the provided thematic areas.
  • Teams must identify and define their own Problem Statement (PS) within the selected thematic area.
  • Teams must build and demonstrate their solution within 24 hours.
  • 2 progress reviews will be conducted.

STEM EDUCATION & LEARNING

Solutions should focus on improving STEM education for school students, rural students, and students from underserved/backward communities.

Key Subject Areas

  • Mathematics
  • Biology
  • Chemistry
  • ️ Physics

Possible Solution Directions

  • Interactive STEM learning
  • Educational software
  • VR/AR-based learning
  • Digital/virtual laboratories
  • Gamified STEM education
  • Innovative education models
  • Experiential and activity-based learning
  • Technology-enabled STEM learning

Development Rules

  • Teams will bring and define their own Problem Statement based on the selected thematic area.
  • Any technology stack can be used.
  • Core solution must be substantially developed during the hackathon.
  • Open-source tools, APIs, datasets and AI-assisted development are permitted where applicable.
  • Teams must disclose significant pre-existing components.
  • All team members must understand and be able to explain their project.

Evaluation Criteria

  • Problem Identification & Understanding
  • Innovation & Creativity
  • STEM Education Impact
  • Technical Implementation
  • Working MVP/Demo
  • Accessibility & Inclusivity
  • Impact & Scalability
  • Presentation & Q&A

️ Important

  • The solution should primarily address STEM education for school students, especially rural and underserved communities.
  • Teams must clearly demonstrate how their solution addresses the identified educational problem.
  • Plagiarism, cheating, misrepresentation, unsafe conduct, or interference with other teams can lead to disqualification.
  • Follow all organizer, jury, venue and safety instructions.

Prize Pool — ₹45,000

1st — ₹20,000
2nd — ₹15,000
3rd — ₹10,000

INNOVATE • BUILD • IMPACT

Presidency University | Presidency Makerspace
